page: Microsoft Azure DC32ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor offering 32 dedicated vCPUs spread across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, BMI2, and FMA.

Integrated local storage is bundled directly into the instance via a 1288 GB SSD disk, providing high-capacity scratch space without relying solely on remote block storage. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the DC32ads_v5 demonstrates consistent middle-tier throughput, recording 1,992.58 on stress-ng single-core and 37,152.51 on multi-core tests. PassMark testing confirms this baseline with an overall CPU score of 34,531.63, driven by balanced performance across extended instruction sets and cryptographic operations, while memory testing yields a score of 2,163.67.

In operational database simulations, the instance delivers steady throughput, producing 12,307.66 operations on PassMark database benchmarks and 29.7 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. The combination of dedicated compute threads, 128 GB memory capacity, and integrated fast local SSD makes it suitable for intermediate data stores, relational databases, CI/CD pipeline orchestration, and general-purpose business applications requiring steady multi-threaded execution.
description: Microsoft Azure DC32ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1288 GB local SSD. It maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB per thread. Benchmark evaluations position the instance firmly in the middle 50% category, producing a multi-core stress-ng result of 37,152.51 and a PassMark CPU score of 34,531.63. Cryptographic performance is accelerated by hardware AES and SHA extensions. Application-level metrics register 29.7 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 12,307.66 in PassMark database benchmarks. With no attached GPU, the instance offers balanced compute density and internal storage capacity suitable for enterprise relational databases, caching layers, and multi-tenant application serving.
